extracted.intended_audience: prospective contributors to Timothy McSweeney’s Quarterly Concern (writers submitting fiction/nonfiction/letters/flash/etc.)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission guidelines for writers sending unsolicited work to Timothy McSweeney’s Quarterly Concern, covering what to send, formatting, cover letters, rights, payment, and response expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited submissions / mailing address
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send unsolicited submissions to McSweeney’s Quarterly c/o Rita Bullwinkel 849 Valencia St. San Francisco CA 94110.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We gladly consider unsolicited works. If you would like a response please include a self-addressed and pre-stamped postcard. We are unable to return manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time / patience
rubrics_metrics.description: Because we are a very small organization with an even smaller editorial department, it often takes us a long time to respond to our submitters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We appreciate your patience with us as we work on getting to your piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and subject
rubrics_metrics.description: We publish mostly fiction and some nonfiction. There are no rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best way to get a sense of what we’re interested in publishing is to read the Quarterly (pick up a subscription or back issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No explicit length limits are imposed by the Quarterly; submit what you think is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They like to hear from people who like the magazine. They are not concerned about writing degrees or past publications, so don’t be daunted if you don’t have an MFA or much in the way of previously published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website submissions are separate
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions for the website should be sent to a different address, following different guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Website submission guidelines are presented in a different link on the site; do not mix Quarterly and website submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s better if you don’t use colors or Fun Fonts or strange formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simple, conventional manuscript formatting rather than decorative or nonstandard styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author bios
rubrics_metrics.description: Feel free to include a brief biography of yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short author bio is optional and permitted alongside submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously published work
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously published work will not be considered here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only original, unpublished work for the Quarterly.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy / no AI-assisted writing
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept no writing aided in any manner by AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before publishing any writing—from a letter to a book-length work—authors published at McSweeney’s will be asked to attest that AI played no part in the creation or writing of that work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors are paid at the time of publication, and our standard rate for short stories is $400.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee for letters, flash fiction, translations, and other formats and situations varies according to circumstances, with equity in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry can be wonderful, but is not something we often publish in the Quarterly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry submissions are less commonly accepted; expect lower likelihood of publication for poetry in the Quarterly.
